description: Baseline comparison across two monitor threads (16 subtrees: 12 from thread 736b1b30 + 4 from thread 0dfc0e00) to identify where deepseek-v4-flash falls short of gpt-5.4-mini. The goal is buyer-utility: the identification step must surface EVERY comment that a future buyer would want attributed to a product — including anaphoric references, same-author continuations, informal endorsements, and variant-specific mentions. Missing a real product reference loses buyer signal downstream; hallucinating a product poisons reviews. Thread 736b1b30 stress-tests: (a) OP subtree with 6 named products in one dense comment; (b) deep reply chains with repeated endorsements across 5+ nesting levels; (c) anaphoric/pronominal references ('both are solid', 'the LG', 'this monitor'); (d) 175 Hz vs 240 Hz variant confusion (MAG 341CQP vs MPG 341CQPX); (e) tangential owner-history mentions vs real evaluations; (f) jokes, thanks, meta-replies that must produce empty products arrays. Thread 0dfc0e00 stress-tests Samsung-variant disambiguation: G8 / G85SD / Odyssey OLED G8 SB / S34DG850SU / S32DG802SU variant name noise across 4 subtrees, where verbatim preservation matters (commenter's spelling must not be silently upgraded).

expectations.desiredOutcome: The identification step must surface EVERY buyer-relevant product reference — the same standard the extraction step applies to quotes. Buyer-relevant means: a future buyer would learn something from knowing this comment is about this product. That includes: owner verdicts (even informal ones like 'all I can say is wow'), reasoned concerns from prospective buyers ('biggest concern is G-sync'), reference-tier informational claims ('TFT says it's the MSI', 'firmware update fixes the HDR'), comparisons ('better panel at a lower price'), issue reports, and anti-recommendations. Missing any of these drops buyer signal from the downstream extraction step. Schema-valid JSON conforming to subtree-identification.schema for every subtree. Every PLAN comment has an entry even when products is empty. Anaphoric and pronominal references resolve to brand+model when the surrounding subtree makes the referent unambiguous — including same-author earlier [PLAN] nodes, not only direct [CONTEXT] parents. Verbatim model preservation: the commenter's own spelling is kept ('34GS9QE' is NOT silently upgraded to '34GS95QE-B', 'G8sd' is not upgraded to 'S34DG850SU'). Variant differentiation: 175 Hz MAG 341CQP is NOT collapsed into 240 Hz MPG 341CQPX. contentQuality is calibrated: 'high' = substantive evaluation with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth ('it's great', 'solid monitor'); 'low' = product named but not evaluated (bare ownership, listing, availability question, anti-recommendation with no reason). When borderline, pick the lower level. Generic brand or panel-tech statements ('OLED panels in general', 'Samsung tends to…') do NOT produce product entries.

goldenOutput.note: Hand-curated Opus reference across all 16 subtrees (12 from thread 736b1b30 + 4 from thread 0dfc0e00). Authoritative signals: (1) verbatim model spelling preserved — '34GS9QE' not upgraded to '34GS95QE-B', 'MPG341' not upgraded to 'MPG 341CQPX', 'G8sd'/'SD'/'SB' not upgraded to S34DG850SU; (2) same-author anaphor chains resolved — makemesplooge's c1 sets context for c3 enthusiasm; Tyrein's '34GS9QE' in st4-c7 carried through to st4-c9; (3) informal endorsements retained ('all I can say is wow', 'absolutely insane') as medium quality; (4) pure questions, social replies, [removed], settings dumps, and bare logistics produce empty arrays; (5) contentQuality errs lower when borderline — anti-recs with no reason are low, short verdicts without specifics are medium not high. The golden is keyed by subtreeId, not inputId — the runner must look up by subtreeId regardless of which input it came from.

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on three dimensions, each 1-10. The goal is buyer-utility: every comment a future buyer would want attributed to a product must be captured — missing a real reference loses downstream extraction signal; hallucinating a product corrupts it. (1) faithfulness (weight: highest) — every buyer-relevant product reference in each PLAN comment is surfaced, including: anaphoric and pronominal references ('both are solid', 'the LG', 'this monitor'); same-author chains via earlier [PLAN] nodes (not only direct [CONTEXT] parents); informal owner endorsements ('all I can say is wow', 'absolutely insane'); reasoned concerns from prospective buyers ('biggest concern is G-sync', 'feeling like a huge gamble'); reference-tier informational claims ('TFT says it's the MSI', 'firmware update fixes the HDR'); anti-recommendations. Verbatim model preservation is part of faithfulness: the commenter's own spelling must be kept — silently upgrading '34GS9QE' to '34GS95QE-B' or 'G8sd' to 'S34DG850SU' is a faithfulness deduction. No products hallucinated from generic brand or panel-tech statements. (2) calibration (weight: medium) — contentQuality matches depth per the schema enum: 'high' = substantive evaluation with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth ('it's great', 'solid monitor'); 'low' = product named but not evaluated. Borderline cases should err lower. Variant accuracy (MAG 341CQP at 175 Hz vs MPG 341CQPX at 240 Hz; G85SD vs S34DG850SU) also counts here. (3) completeness (weight: low) — every PLAN comment has an entry even when products is empty; jokes/thanks/meta-replies produce empty arrays without inventing products. Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness,calibration,completeness}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'. In the rationale, call out specific subtrees and comment IDs where the candidates diverge — that is the most actionable signal for prompt iteration.
